<reason>A established why commercial nonviability need not imply poor public value, while defending selective, technology-neutral funding rather than automatic subsidies. Its construction-versus-operating-cost distinction forced B to concede that sustainable networks can remain unbuilt, weakening the voucher alternative. A also answered both pressure questions directly and exposed waiting for technology as another uncertain forecast. B raised legitimate appraisal and opportunity-cost concerns, but repeatedly substituted absolute objections for comparative analysis and mischaracterized “even when” as an automatic spending trigger.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest challenge was that verifying a working connection does not establish its value. A answered by separating delivery verification from conservative appraisal and identifying reviewable outcomes. B’s closing then falsely treated A’s acknowledgment of uncertainty as a concession that safeguards cannot address error.</best_rebuttal>
